1.title: The Four Dimensions and External Factors
1.text: Welcome to Module four: The Four Dimensions and External Factors. It covers the exam area The eye til Four Dimensions of Product and Service Management. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. List the four dimensions. Understand the importance of each. Explain the holistic approach. Know the external factors (pestle). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The eye til Four Dimensions of Product and Service Management (ten percent). Exam format: forty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; twenty-six correct answers (sixty-five percent) pass. Validated against: the official eye til Foundation (Version five) syllabus, version five point zero (February two thousand twenty-six).

1.title: Why four dimensions
1.text: Why four dimensions. Every product and service must be looked at through four dimensions at the same time. If one is ignored, value suffers. This is the holistic approach: think about all four together, not one at a time. Organizations and people. Structure, roles, culture, skills, leadership, communication. Information and technology. Data, knowledge, tools, platforms, automation, A I. Partners and suppliers. Relationships with other organizations that supply or support the work. Value streams and processes. The activities and flows that turn demand into value.

1.title: Why four dimensions, continued
1.text: Why four dimensions. The figure shows this: The four dimensions surrounded by the external factors.

1.title: Why four dimensions, continued
1.text: Why four dimensions. eye til four called these the "four dimensions of service management". Version five says product and service management.

1.title: Each dimension in a little more detail
1.text: Each dimension in a little more detail. Organizations and people. Typical questions: Who does what? Do they have the skills? Is the culture right? Example: Cross-functional product teams, clear roles, training. Information and technology. Typical questions: What information and tools are needed? Is data protected and usable? Example: A monitoring platform, a knowledge base, A I assistants. Partners and suppliers. Typical questions: Which outside parties are involved? How are contracts and relationships managed? Example: A cloud provider, a development partner.

1.title: Each dimension in a little more detail, continued
1.text: Each dimension in a little more detail. Value streams and processes. Typical questions: What steps create value? Where are the waits and waste? Example: A request-to-fulfillment flow with automation. Exam tip: People and culture equals organizations and people. Tools and data equals information and technology. Outside parties equals partners and suppliers. Steps and flow equals value streams and processes.

1.title: External factors: PESTLE
1.text: External factors: pestle (political, economic, social, technological, legal and environmental). The dimensions are influenced from outside. pestle lists the external factors. P. Factor: Political. Example: Government policy, trade rules. E. Factor: Economic. Example: Inflation, exchange rates, funding. S. Factor: Social. Example: Customer expectations, working habits. T. Factor: Technological. Example: New tools, A I, standards. L. Factor: Legal. Example: Privacy and data laws, contracts. E. Factor: Environmental. Example: Climate rules, energy use. Exam tip: pestle equals Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal, Environmental. The list is for external factors; internal factors are the four dimensions themselves.

1.title: External factors: PESTLE, continued
1.text: External factors: pestle. Exam tip: If an option names a dimension that is not one of the four (for example "governance" or "practices"), it is a distractor. Only organizations and people, information and technology, partners and suppliers, value streams and processes count.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A team has the right tools but nobody trained to use them. Which dimension is weakest? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Organizations and people. Skills and roles belong to organizations and people.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which statement about the four dimensions is C O R R E C T? (one) They should be considered together. (two) One dimension can be ignored if the others are strong. (three) Partners and suppliers is one of the four. (four) pestle is a list of the four dimensions. The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: one and three. The four dimensions are used together, and partners and suppliers is one of them.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. New privacy legislation forces a change in how customer data is stored. Which pestle factor is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Legal. Laws and regulations are the legal factor.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Identify the missing word(s). The blank dimension covers the activities and flows that turn demand into value. The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Value streams and processes. That describes value streams and processes.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A company relies on an outside vendor to run its help desk. Which dimension does managing that vendor fall under? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Partners and suppliers. Relationships with outside parties are partners and suppliers.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Why does eye til stress a holistic approach to the four dimensions? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: So that all four are balanced and no weak dimension undermines value. Value suffers when any dimension is neglected.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. List the four dimensions. Answer: Organizations and people; information and technology; partners and suppliers; value streams and processes. Question two. What does pestle stand for? Answer: Political, economic, social, technological, legal, environmental. Question three. Which dimension covers data, tools and A I? Answer: Information and technology.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which dimension covers culture and skills? Answer: Organizations and people. Question five. What is the holistic approach? Answer: Considering all four dimensions together. Question six. Are pestle factors internal or external? Answer: External.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Four dimensions: organizations and people; information and technology; partners and suppliers; value streams and processes. Holistic: all four together. pestle: political, economic, social, technological, legal, environmental (external). Old wording: "four dimensions of service management".
